message.content:
You are the implementer subagent for **Task A4** of the multi-vehicle concurrency plan.

Repo: /home/ubuntu/个人学习/amr_dispatcher, branch `feat/multi-vehicle-concurrency` (already checked out; commit your work there).
Plan: /home/ubuntu/.claude/plans/fizzy-sparking-ripple.md — read the "P0.6 ROS 话题与 TF 隔离" and "A4" sections.

## Goal
Parameterize the motion-control chain so **multiple vehicles can run concurrently** without cross-talk, while keeping **single-vehicle behavior byte-identical** (compatibility red line).

Topic convention (per vehicle `vid`):
- `/plan/{vid}` — planned path
- `/cmd_vel_raw/{vid}` — tracker output
- `/cmd_vel_safe/{vid}` — safety-gate output
- `/odom/{vid}` — chassis odometry
- `/tracking/error/{vid}` — tracking error / arrived

**Compatibility red line**: with no `vehicle_id` configured (default), every topic name must stay EXACTLY as today (`/plan`, `/cmd_vel_raw`, `/cmd_vel_safe`, `/odom`, `/tracking/error`). The existing e2e (`./scripts/check_vda5050_e2e.sh`) must pass unchanged.

## Files to change

### 1. `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/path_tracker_node.cpp` + header
- New parameter `vehicle_id` (default `""` = legacy single-vehicle).
- New parameters allowing explicit override: `plan_topic`, `odom_topic`, `cmd_vel_topic`, `tracking_error_topic` (each default `""` = derive from `vehicle_id`).
- Derivation rule: if `vehicle_id` empty → use the legacy global names exactly. If `vehicle_id` non-empty → `/plan/{vid}`, `/cmd_vel_raw/{vid}`, `/odom/{vid}`, `/tracking/error/{vid}`.
- Explicit overrides win over derivation.
- Keep the heartbeat topic `/safety/heartbeat/path_tracker` as-is for the default case; for per-vehicle mode use `/safety/heartbeat/path_tracker/{vid}` **but** also keep publishing to the legacy topic when `vehicle_id` is empty. NOTE: the safety gate subscribes to the heartbeat topic; make the pairing symmetric (see safety gate below) — a per-vehicle gate instance must watch the per-vehicle tracker heartbeat.

### 2. `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/safety_gate_node.cpp` + header
- New parameter `vehicle_id` (default `""`).
- New parameters `raw_cmd_vel_topic`, `safe_cmd_vel_topic`, `chassis_heartbeat_topic`, `path_tracker_heartbeat_topic`, `teleop_cmd_vel_topic`, `estop_topic`, `bumper_topic`, `manual_takeover_topic`, `link_health_topic`, `safety_state_topic` (all default `""` = derive).
- Derivation: legacy names when `vehicle_id` empty; `/cmd_vel_raw/{vid}`, `/cmd_vel_safe/{vid}`, `/safety/heartbeat/chassis_driver/{vid}`, `/safety/heartbeat/path_tracker/{vid}`, `/safety/estop/{vid}`, `/safety/bumper/{vid}`, `/safety/manual_takeover/{vid}`, `/chassis/link_health/{vid}`, `/safety/state/{vid}` when set.
- The `watched_nodes_` list contains literal names "chassis_driver" / "path_tracker" — the watchdog source identity. For per-vehicle mode, keep the source identity strings stable but make the SUBSCRIBED TOPIC per-vehicle. Read `SafetyWatchdog::FeedHeartbeat(source)` and make sure the per-vehicle gate feeds the same source names.
- **Important**: `/safety/estop` and `/safety/bumper` are *global safety* signals in practice — a per-vehicle gate should still receive the GLOBAL estop topic (an emergency stop anywhere must stop every vehicle). Decide and document: recommended = subscribe BOTH the global `/safety/estop` and the per-vehicle `/safety/estop/{vid}` (global always honored). Implement that.

### 3. `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/chassis_driver_node.cpp` + header
- New parameters `cmd_vel_topic` (default `""` → `/cmd_vel_safe`), `odom_topic` (default `""` → `/odom`), `link_health_topic` (default `""` → `/chassis/link_health`), `heartbeat_topic` (default `""` → `/safety/heartbeat/chassis_driver`), `vehicle_id` (default `""`).
- With `vehicle_id` set: derive `/cmd_vel_safe/{vid}`, `/odom/{vid}`, `/chassis/link_health/{vid}`, `/safety/heartbeat/chassis_driver/{vid}`.
- Also parameterize the TF frame names: `odom_frame_id` / `base_frame_id` defaults stay `/odom` and `/base_link`; for per-vehicle mode derive `{vid}/odom` and `{vid}/base_link` **only if the params are left at their defaults** (i.e. derive when the user did not override). Simplest acceptable approach: add new params `odom_frame_prefix` / `base_frame_prefix` (default `""`), and if `vehicle_id` is set AND the frame params are still the defaults, use `{vid}/odom` / `{vid}/base_link`. Document the rule clearly in a comment. **TF frames must be unique per vehicle** — two vehicles publishing the same `odom` frame is a hard error.

### 4. `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/dispatcher_node.cpp` + header
- New parameter `vehicle_ids` (default `""` = legacy single-vehicle): comma-separated list of vehicle ids this dispatcher manages.
- `plan_pub_` (currently a single `LifecyclePublisher<nav_msgs::msg::Path>` on `/plan`) → keep it for the legacy/default case AND add `vehicle_plan_pubs_` (map vehicle_id → publisher on `/plan/{vid}`). Concretely:
  - Keep `plan_pub_` exactly as-is (default `/plan`) so legacy behavior is untouched.
  - Add `std::unordered_map<std::string, rclcpp::LifecyclePublisher<nav_msgs::msg::Path>::SharedPtr> vehicle_plan_pubs_`.
  - Add a helper `PublishPlanForVehicle(const std::string& vehicle_id, const nav_msgs::msg::Path& path)` that publishes to `/plan/{vid}` when `vehicle_id` is non-empty, else to `plan_pub_`.
  - Add a helper `PlanPublisherForVehicle(const std::string& vehicle_id)` returning the right publisher.
- `/odom` subscription → keep the global one; add per-vehicle `/odom/{vid}` subscriptions for the ids in `vehicle_ids`, each updating a `vehicle_poses_[vid]` map (Pose2D + has_odom flag). Keep `current_pose_`/`has_odom_` updated from the GLOBAL `/odom` as today (legacy path).
- `/tracking/error` subscription → keep the global one; add per-vehicle `/tracking/error/{vid}` subscriptions. **Do not yet change the completion semantics** (that is Task A5); just add the subscriptions and route them to a per-vehicle callback that you stub with a clear TODO comment naming the A5 task, or — better — implement a per-vehicle callback `TrackingErrorCbForVehicle(vehicle_id, msg)` that currently only logs, with a clear comment that A5 will route it to mission completion. Keep the legacy global callback behavior EXACTLY as-is.
- IMPORTANT: the node is a lifecycle node — new publishers/subscriptions must be created in `on_configure` and reset in `on_cleanup` (follow the existing patterns).

### 5. `launch/full_system.launch.py`
- New launch argument `vehicle_ids` (default `""` = legacy).
- When non-empty: for each id, launch a `path_tracker_node` + `safety_gate_node` + `chassis_driver_node` group with `vehicle_id:="<id>"` and namespace isolation (`namespace="<id>"` would break the absolute topic names — instead set the explicit per-vehicle topic parameters and keep namespace empty, OR use namespace + relative topics. **Choose one approach and make it consistent**; recommended: keep namespace empty and use explicit absolute per-vehicle topic names, since the topic names already carry the vehicle id).
- **Do not** change the default (empty) launch behavior in any way.
- The `chassis_driver_node` in a multi-vehicle setup needs a distinct `serial_device` per vehicle — add a launch arg `serial_devices` (comma-separated) OR derive `serial_device` as the existing default + `/<vid>`. Document the choice. Note the default single-vehicle path must be unchanged.

## Constraints
- ROS 2 topic names must be valid; vehicle ids coming from config must be validated (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`). If an id is invalid, skip that vehicle with a WARN (do not crash).
- Everything in `amr_dispatcher_core` stays untouched (zero-ROS invariant).
- Do NOT implement mission→vehicle selection or multi-vehicle mission completion (that is A5/A6). Your job is the topic/TF isolation layer.

## Verification (mandatory)
1. Container build: `docker exec amr_dispatcher bash -c "source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && cd /workspace && colcon build --packages-select amr_dispatcher_core amr_dispatcher_ros --base-paths src"` (build core first if needed; `--base-paths src` from `/workspace` is required for package discovery).
2. Core tests unchanged: `ctest --test-dir build/core` → 648/648 (or whatever it is now — report the number).
3. **Compatibility red line**: `./scripts/check_vda5050_e2e.sh` → all 8 stages PASS, EXIT=0. Paste the summary block.
4. Manual spot check: with `vehicle_ids` set (e.g. `amr_01,amr_02`), confirm the two tracker instances subscribe to different topics (you can inspect `ros2 topic list` in the container, or just show the log lines the nodes print with their resolved topic names — make the nodes LOG their resolved topic names at startup, that doubles as evidence).

## Commit
`feat(ros): 运动控制链 per-vehicle 话题与 TF 隔离（多车并发基础）`
End with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

## Report back
Files touched, commit SHA, the exact topic-derivation rules you implemented, the TF-frame uniqueness rule, build + test + e2e evidence, and a precise list of the member variables / helper functions A5 and A6 will need (e.g. `vehicle_plan_pubs_`, `vehicle_poses_`, `PublishPlanForVehicle`, `TrackingErrorCbForVehicle`).

1	# 多车车队化实施计划 v2（评审修订版）
2	
3	> 修订依据：评审提出的 6 个关键问题 + 5 个实施坑。**P0 先冻结接口契约**，再 A → C → B。
4	> 相对 v1 的核心变化：**执行后端分离**（local_sim vs vda5050）、**选车三态结果**、**强清改隔离而非摘除**、**结构化车辆状态消息**。
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	VDA 5050 车队适配 Epic（Tasks 1–7）已合并 main 并推送。核心 612/612 单测绿、e2e 8 阶段全 PASS。
9	剩余缺口决定"多车车队"能否真正落地：真多车并发、显式绑定选车、时空窗交通协调、Web 强清入口。
10	
11	**评审否决项（必须先修正）**：
12	1. VDA 5050 车辆与本地模拟车辆的执行模型混同 → 必须**执行后端分离**
13	2. `Mission.fleet_id` 语义被挪用 → 必须**新增** `assigned_vehicle_id`
14	3. 选车输入数据源未闭合 → 静态配置 + 动态状态**分离**，位置不可用即**不合格**
15	4. 选车失败 vs 排队矛盾 → 结果必须**三态**
16	5. 时空窗安全模型不完整 → 逐边进出时刻 + 全有或全无 + 延期扩窗
17	6. 强清把"通信失联"直接等同于"可释放路权" → 必须**隔离态 + 审计 + 服务端复验**
18	
19	---
20	
21	## P0：接口契约冻结（先做，产出设计文档 + 核心类型）
22	
23	产出 `docs/superpowers/specs/multi_vehicle_fleet.md`（契约文档），并落地以下核心类型（零 ROS）：
24	
25	### P0.1 车辆执行后端分离（评审问题 1）
26	```cpp
27	enum class VehicleExecutionBackend {
28	  kLocalSim,   // 本地模拟车：调度发 /plan/{vid}，path_tracker 算 cmd_vel，chassis 执行
29	  kVda5050,    // 外部 VDA 5050 车：调度只发 MQTT order，车辆自带控制器执行
30	};
31	```
32	- **铁律**：`kVda5050` 车辆**不启动** path_tracker / safety_gate / chassis 三件套，也**不订阅** `/plan/{vid}`、不产生 `/cmd_vel_raw/{vid}`。
33	- 两者**共用**：任务队列、选车、路权锁、动态解锁、断链守卫、订单构建。
34	- 两者**不共用**：底层运动控制链。
35	- VDA 5050 车辆的"完成"判定 = state 报文 `lastNodeId` 推进到订单终点（`/fleet/{vid}/state`），**不是** `/tracking/error` 的 arrived。
36	- 车辆清单来源：`config/fleet.yaml` 的 `robots[]` 增加 `backend: local_sim|vda5050` 字段（默认 `local_sim`），`id` 即 vehicle_id。
37	
38	### P0.2 车辆身份语义分离（评审问题 2）
39	| 概念 | 载体 | 说明 |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| 车队归属 | `Mission.fleet_id` | **保持原义**（"V1.2 多机预留"），不挪用 |
42	| 承接车辆 | `Mission.assigned_vehicle_id` | **新增字段**，空 = 待选车 |
43	| 车辆 | `VehicleRuntimeState.vehicle_id` | 对应 `fleet.yaml` 的 `robots[].id` / VDA 5050 serialNumber |
44	
45	- `SubmitOrder.srv` / `EnqueueMission.srv` **末尾追加** `string assigned_vehicle_id`（不复用 `vehicle_id` 命名，避免与"车队/机器人 id"混读）。
46	- **兼容性不假设**：ROS 2 srv 变更后旧客户端行为需**实测**（用仓库内现有客户端/脚本），不靠推断。验证方式：e2e 现有 8 阶段 + 现有 REST 提单链路（它们就是旧客户端）。
47	
48	### P0.3 选车输入数据源闭合 + 三态结果（评审问题 3、4）
49	```cpp
50	struct VehicleRuntimeState {
51	  std::string vehicle_id;
52	  VehicleExecutionBackend backend = VehicleExecutionBackend::kLocalSim;
53	  // —— 静态（来自 fleet.yaml）——
54	  bool enabled = true;
55	  std::vector<std::string> capabilities;   // 空 = 未声明限制
56	  // —— 动态（来自最新状态报文，带时间戳）——
57	  bool online = true;
58	  bool busy = false;
59	  double battery_percent = 100.0;
60	  bool position_valid = false;             // 位置是否可信
61	  std::string current_station_id;          // 有效位置对应的站点
62	  std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point state_time{};  // 状态新鲜度
63	  bool quarantined = false;                // 隔离态（强清后）——不合格但可恢复
64	};
65	
66	enum class AssignmentOutcome {
67	  kAssigned,        // 已选车
68	  kDeferred,        // 暂时不可用（车忙/位置陈旧/状态未到）→ 任务留队等待
69	  kIndeterminate,   // 状态不确定（无该车状态报文）→ 暂停自动分配，等状态恢复
70	  kRejected,        // 永久不满足（显式指定车不存在/禁用/能力不符/隔离）→ 拒绝
71	};
72	```
73	**硬约束**（`kAssigned` 必须全部满足，显式指定同样适用）：
74	`online ∧ enabled ∧ !busy ∧ !quarantined ∧ 具备能力 ∧ battery ≥ 阈值 ∧ position_valid ∧ 状态新鲜`
75	
76	**距离**：优先**路网路径成本**（`PlanMissionRouteLocks` / `FindRoutePath` 同源的 `RouteOrEuclideanDistance`），欧氏距离仅在路径不可算时作为**次级**度量；**位置无效或状态陈旧 → 该车不合格**（不再"first_available"兜底派单）。
77	
78	**去重既有能力**：`core/fleet/fleet_catalog.cpp` 已有 `SelectFleetRobotForStationTask`（路网距离 + 电池 tiebreak），**复用其距离计算**，不重复造。
79	
80	### P0.4 车辆状态结构化消息（评审坑 5）
81	- 新增 `msg/VehicleLinkState.msg`（**不用平行数组**）：
82	  ```
83	  string vehicle_id
84	  string backend            # local_sim | vda5050
85	  bool online
86	  bool busy
87	  bool quarantined
88	  bool position_valid
89	  string current_station_id
90	  double battery_percent
91	  int64 state_age_ms
92	  string last_error
93	  ```
94	- `DispatcherState.msg` 末尾追加 `VehicleLinkState[] vda5050_vehicle_links`（替代评审否决的平行数组方案）。
95	
96	### P0.5 强清安全边界（评审问题 6）
97	- 强清**不摘车**，改为**隔离**：`quarantined = true` → 该车**不再参与自动分配**（`PlanVehicleAssignment` 视为不合格），但仍在受管清单、仍可见、仍可被显式恢复。
98	- **恢复流程**：新增 `RestoreVda5050Link` 服务——需操作员确认车辆位置已核实（`position_verified` 字段）→ 清 `quarantined` → 重新参与分配。
99	- **审计**：`ForceClearVda5050Link.srv` 增加 `operator_id`（必填）、`reason`（必填）、`confirm_vehicle_id`（必须与 `vehicle_id` 完全一致，防误操作）。
100	- **服务端复验**：前端按钮隐藏**不是**安全边界；服务端 `PlanForceClearLink` 重新校验（在线车拒、隔离车拒、车辆 id 必须匹配）。
101	- **车辆物理占位未知**：强清释放锁前必须显式记录"车辆物理位置未核实"这一事实到审计日志（不伪称已确认安全）。
102	
103	### P0.6 ROS 话题与 TF 隔离（评审坑 1、2）
104	- 话题命名：`/plan/{vid}`、`/cmd_vel_raw/{vid}`、`/cmd_vel_safe/{vid}`、`/odom/{vid}`、`/tracking/error/{vid}`。
105	- **vehicle_id 必须先过 ROS 名称校验**（`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`），非法 id 直接拒绝接入（外部 VDA 5050 serialNumber 不保证合法）。
106	- **TF frame 隔离**：每车 `odom_frame_id` / `base_frame_id` 唯一（如 `amr_01/odom`、`amr_01/base_link`），禁止多车抢同一 frame。
107	- 兼容红线：单车（`vehicle_ids` 为空）时**话题名逐字不变**。
108	
109	### P0.7 并发派单原子性（评审坑 3）
110	- 派发链路的提交顺序固定为：**选车 → 占车（busy）→ 预留路权锁 → Pop 出队 → 发布订单/路径**。
111	- 任一步失败 → **逆序回滚**（释放 busy、回滚锁预留、任务留队），**禁止**出现"车被占但任务没派"或"锁被占但车没占"。
112	- 单线程 executor（现状 `rclcpp::spin`）保证无竞态，但**回滚必须写全**。
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Task A：真多车并发 + 显式绑定（评审后修订）
117	
118	### A1 — 核心纯函数（已部分实现，按评审修订）
119	文件：`core/fleet/vehicle_assignment.hpp/.cpp`（已存在 `b6b3538`，需按 P0.3 修订）
120	- 修订点：①加 `backend`/`quarantined`/`position_valid`/`state_time` 字段；②结果改三态 `AssignmentOutcome`；③**删除** "first_available 兜底"（位置不可算 → 该车不合格）；④显式指定也施加全部硬约束；⑤加 `state_max_age_ms` 阈值（默认 5000，超龄 → 状态不确定 → `kIndeterminate`）。
121	- `test/unit/test_vehicle_assignment.cpp` 已有 24 例，需按新语义增补：三态各一例、隔离车不合格、位置无效不合格、状态超龄 → indeterminate、显式指定带全部硬约束。
122	
123	### A2 — 车辆身份字段
124	- `mission_state.hpp`：`fleet_id` **保持原义**，**新增** `std::string assigned_vehicle_id;`
125	- `SubmitOrder.srv` / `EnqueueMission.srv`：末尾追加 `string assigned_vehicle_id`。
126	- `dispatcher_node.cpp`：`SubmitOrderCb` / `EnqueueMissionCb` 写入 `m.assigned_vehicle_id`。
127	- `rest_gateway.cpp`：`/api/v1/orders` 解析 `vehicle=` query 参数透传。
128	
129	### A3 — 车队目录接入 + 车辆状态表
130	- `fleet.yaml`：`robots[]` 增 `backend` 字段（默认 `local_sim`）。
131	- `dispatcher_node`：`on_configure` 加载 `config/fleet.yaml`（参数 `fleet_catalog_file`），构建 `vehicle_states_`（vehicle_id → VehicleRuntimeState）。
132	- 动态刷新：VDA 5050 车从 `/fleet/{vid}/state` 更新 online/battery/position/state_time；本地车从 `/odom/{vid}` 更新位置。
133	- 隔离态：`quarantined` 由强清/恢复服务维护。
134	
135	### A4 — per-vehicle 话题参数化（**仅 local_sim 后端的车**）
136	- `path_tracker_node`：参数 `vehicle_id`（默认空 = 单车兼容）+ 话题可覆盖。
137	- `safety_gate_node`：参数 `vehicle_id` + 话题可覆盖。
138	- `chassis_driver_node`：参数 `cmd_vel_topic` / `odom_topic` / frame 前缀。
139	- `dispatcher_node`：`plan_pub_` → `vehicle_plan_pubs_[vid]`；`/tracking/error/{vid}`、`/odom/{vid}` per-vehicle 订阅。
140	- `launch/full_system.launch.py`：`vehicle_ids` 参数（非空时按 local_sim 车起多组 tracker/gate/chassis，namespace 隔离）。
141	
142	### A5 — 多车执行槽位拆分
143	- `tracking_mission_id_`（string）→ `tracking_missions_`（mission_id → vehicle_id）+ `vehicle_current_mission_`（vehicle_id → mission_id）。
144	- 派发门控：**只对 `kLocalSim` 车**要求 slot 空闲；`kVda5050` 车的"执行中"由订单状态判定，不占 path_tracker slot。
145	- `TrackingErrorCb`（local_sim 到达）按 vehicle_id 收口；VDA 5050 完成判定在 `Vda5050StateCb`（lastNodeId 到终点）。
146	- `EnforceVda5050LinkGuard`：fleet-wide 挂起 → **按车挂起**。
147	
148	### A6 — 选车接线（tri-state）
149	- 派发时：`assigned_vehicle_id` 空 → 调 `PlanVehicleAssignment`。
150	  - `kAssigned` → 继续派发
151	  - `kDeferred` → **任务留队**（不 FailMission！），记 `pending_wait_`，下 tick 重试
152	  - `kIndeterminate` → 暂停自动派发（WARN），等状态恢复
153	  - `kRejected` → `FailMission` 带明确原因
154	- **队首阻塞**：队首任务不可派时，**继续扫描队列后续任务**找可派发的（需 core 支持 peek-N 或 snapshot 后逐个尝试）。
155	
156	### A7 — 验证
157	- 核心单测：A1 修订后的用例 + A2 字段 + 派发 tri-state 决策单测。
158	- **e2e 回归（兼容红线）**：单车配置下现有 8 阶段原样 PASS。
159	- **e2e 新增 Stage 7（本地双模拟车）**：两台 local_sim 车各起一组 tracker/gate/chassis，提交 2 单 → 断言两车**同时**在跑（时间窗重叠断言）、状态不串线、锁无交叉误释放、两单都完成。
160	- **e2e 新增 Stage 8（双 VDA 5050 车）**：两台 mock VDA 车（`mock_amr_01`/`mock_amr_02`）+ 订单路由 → 断言两车各自收到 order、state 互不串线、两单都完成、锁正确释放。**不允许**用两套 ROS tracker 冒充 VDA 5050 多车闭环。
161

164	## Task C：Web 强清闭环（评审后修订）
165	
166	### C1 — 服务语义修订
167	- `ForceClearVda5050Link.srv` 增：`operator_id`（必填）、`confirm_vehicle_id`（必填，须等于 `vehicle_id`）。
168	- 响应增：`quarantined`（车已隔离）、`audit_id`。
169	- 新增 `RestoreVda5050Link.srv`：`vehicle_id` + `operator_id` + `position_verified`（bool）→ 解除隔离。
170	- `PlanForceClearLink`（核心纯函数）按 P0.5 修订：在线拒、隔离拒、id 不匹配拒；受理 → 释锁 + 收口在途任务 + **置隔离**（非移除）。
171	
172	### C2 — REST 端点
173	- `POST /api/v1/force_clear_link`，**请求体 JSON**（非 query）：`{vehicle_id, confirm_vehicle_id, operator_id, reason}`。
174	- `POST /api/v1/restore_link`：同上语义。
175	- `GET /api/v1/vehicle_links`：返回结构化车辆状态（复用 `VehicleLinkState`）。
176	- 危险操作：超时处理 + 审计字段透传 + 失败回传服务端拒绝原因（HTTP 409）。
177	
178	### C3 — Web 控制台
179	- 新增「受管车辆」面板：表格（id / backend / online / busy / quarantined / 位置 / 电量 / 状态时延）。
180	- 强清按钮：**仅对满足服务端条件的车启用**（前端过滤是 UX，服务端仍复验）；点击后**弹确认框**要求填写 operator_id + reason，并回显车辆 id 确认。
181	- 隔离态展示 + 「恢复」按钮（需勾选"已核实车辆位置"）。
182	- 沿用现有 `baseUrl` + fetch 风格。
183	
184	### C4 — 验证
185	- e2e Stage 6.8 扩展：改用 **REST 端点**触发强清，断言 HTTP 响应（含审计 id）+ 锁释放 + 车辆进入隔离 + 后续任务不派给该车。
186	- 新增：恢复流程断言（恢复后重新可派发）。
187	- 控制台手工验证。
188	
189	---
190	
191	## Task B：时空窗交通协调（评审后修订）
192	
193	### B1 — 逐边进出时刻 + 全有或全无
194	- 核心新增 `core/workflow/time_space_planning.hpp/.cpp`：
195	  - 输入：每单的**逐资源**占用区间（每条边单独的 enter/exit 时刻）、资源冲突模型、车辆参数。
196	  - 占用时长 = 路径长度 / 速度 × 安全系数 + **加减速与转弯附加时间** + **车辆尺寸/安全余量**。
197	  - **全有或全无**：一条路径涉及多资源 → 必须**整条路径全部预约成功**才提交；任一失败 → 全部回滚（`ResourceTable` 需补一个批量预约接口，带 rollback）。
198	- 路口/窄道/对向冲突：进入资源模型（不只是同边窗口重叠）——**一期以"节点资源（路口）+ 边资源（通道）双粒度"表达**，节点窗口 = 进入路口到驶出路口的完整区间。
199	
200	### B2 — 延期扩窗（执行偏离时）
201	- 车辆上报进度滞后 → **延长**该车的窗口（`ExtendTimeSpace`），延长失败（与后车窗口冲突）→ 触发**后车让行等待**（延后后车窗口），**绝不**因窗口到期而让后车进入。
202	- **窗口到期 ≠ 资源已释放**：释放仍需"车辆确认驶离该资源"（lastNodeId 推进），与 Spec §5.3 逐段解锁一致。
203	
204	### B3 — 双模式接线
205	- 参数 `traffic_mode: static | time_space`（**默认 static**，现网行为不变）。
206	- `time_space` 模式仅在 Task A 多车并发落地且 B1/B2 单测全绿后**显式启用**。
207	
208	### B4 — 验证
209	- `test/unit/test_time_space_planning.cpp`：逐边窗口、全有或全无回滚、延期扩窗、冲突让行、零时长边界。
210	- `test/integration/`：两单共享边不同窗口 → 双成功；同窗口 → 一成一败（无残留半预约）。
211

236	## 验证总表

# 多车车队化实施计划 v2（评审修订版）

> 修订依据：评审提出的 6 个关键问题 + 5 个实施坑。**P0 先冻结接口契约**，再 A → C → B。
> 相对 v1 的核心变化：**执行后端分离**（local_sim vs vda5050）、**选车三态结果**、**强清改隔离而非摘除**、**结构化车辆状态消息**。

## Context

VDA 5050 车队适配 Epic（Tasks 1–7）已合并 main 并推送。核心 612/612 单测绿、e2e 8 阶段全 PASS。
剩余缺口决定"多车车队"能否真正落地：真多车并发、显式绑定选车、时空窗交通协调、Web 强清入口。

**评审否决项（必须先修正）**：
1. VDA 5050 车辆与本地模拟车辆的执行模型混同 → 必须**执行后端分离**
2. `Mission.fleet_id` 语义被挪用 → 必须**新增** `assigned_vehicle_id`
3. 选车输入数据源未闭合 → 静态配置 + 动态状态**分离**，位置不可用即**不合格**
4. 选车失败 vs 排队矛盾 → 结果必须**三态**
5. 时空窗安全模型不完整 → 逐边进出时刻 + 全有或全无 + 延期扩窗
6. 强清把"通信失联"直接等同于"可释放路权" → 必须**隔离态 + 审计 + 服务端复验**

---

## P0：接口契约冻结（先做，产出设计文档 + 核心类型）

产出 `docs/superpowers/specs/multi_vehicle_fleet.md`（契约文档），并落地以下核心类型（零 ROS）：

### P0.1 车辆执行后端分离（评审问题 1）
```cpp
enum class VehicleExecutionBackend {
  kLocalSim,   // 本地模拟车：调度发 /plan/{vid}，path_tracker 算 cmd_vel，chassis 执行
  kVda5050,    // 外部 VDA 5050 车：调度只发 MQTT order，车辆自带控制器执行
};
```
- **铁律**：`kVda5050` 车辆**不启动** path_tracker / safety_gate / chassis 三件套，也**不订阅** `/plan/{vid}`、不产生 `/cmd_vel_raw/{vid}`。
- 两者**共用**：任务队列、选车、路权锁、动态解锁、断链守卫、订单构建。
- 两者**不共用**：底层运动控制链。
- VDA 5050 车辆的"完成"判定 = state 报文 `lastNodeId` 推进到订单终点（`/fleet/{vid}/state`），**不是** `/tracking/error` 的 arrived。
- 车辆清单来源：`config/fleet.yaml` 的 `robots[]` 增加 `backend: local_sim|vda5050` 字段（默认 `local_sim`），`id` 即 vehicle_id。

### P0.2 车辆身份语义分离（评审问题 2）
| 概念 | 载体 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 车队归属 | `Mission.fleet_id` | **保持原义**（"V1.2 多机预留"），不挪用 |
| 承接车辆 | `Mission.assigned_vehicle_id` | **新增字段**，空 = 待选车 |
| 车辆 | `VehicleRuntimeState.vehicle_id` | 对应 `fleet.yaml` 的 `robots[].id` / VDA 5050 serialNumber |

- `SubmitOrder.srv` / `EnqueueMission.srv` **末尾追加** `string assigned_vehicle_id`（不复用 `vehicle_id` 命名，避免与"车队/机器人 id"混读）。
- **兼容性不假设**：ROS 2 srv 变更后旧客户端行为需**实测**（用仓库内现有客户端/脚本），不靠推断。验证方式：e2e 现有 8 阶段 + 现有 REST 提单链路（它们就是旧客户端）。

### P0.3 选车输入数据源闭合 + 三态结果（评审问题 3、4）
```cpp
struct VehicleRuntimeState {
  std::string vehicle_id;
  VehicleExecutionBackend backend = VehicleExecutionBackend::kLocalSim;
  // —— 静态（来自 fleet.yaml）——
  bool enabled = true;
  std::vector<std::string> capabilities;   // 空 = 未声明限制
  // —— 动态（来自最新状态报文，带时间戳）——
  bool online = true;
  bool busy = false;
  double battery_percent = 100.0;
  bool position_valid = false;             // 位置是否可信
  std::string current_station_id;          // 有效位置对应的站点
  std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point state_time{};  // 状态新鲜度
  bool quarantined = false;                // 隔离态（强清后）——不合格但可恢复
};

enum class AssignmentOutcome {
  kAssigned,        // 已选车
  kDeferred,        // 暂时不可用（车忙/位置陈旧/状态未到）→ 任务留队等待
  kIndeterminate,   // 状态不确定（无该车状态报文）→ 暂停自动分配，等状态恢复
  kRejected,        // 永久不满足（显式指定车不存在/禁用/能力不符/隔离）→ 拒绝
};
```
**硬约束**（`kAssigned` 必须全部满足，显式指定同样适用）：
`online ∧ enabled ∧ !busy ∧ !quarantined ∧ 具备能力 ∧ battery ≥ 阈值 ∧ position_valid ∧ 状态新鲜`

**距离**：优先**路网路径成本**（`PlanMissionRouteLocks` / `FindRoutePath` 同源的 `RouteOrEuclideanDistance`），欧氏距离仅在路径不可算时作为**次级**度量；**位置无效或状态陈旧 → 该车不合格**（不再"first_available"兜底派单）。

**去重既有能力**：`core/fleet/fleet_catalog.cpp` 已有 `SelectFleetRobotForStationTask`（路网距离 + 电池 tiebreak），**复用其距离计算**，不重复造。

### P0.4 车辆状态结构化消息（评审坑 5）
- 新增 `msg/VehicleLinkState.msg`（**不用平行数组**）：
  ```
  string vehicle_id
  string backend            # local_sim | vda5050
  bool online
  bool busy
  bool quarantined
  bool position_valid
  string current_station_id
  double battery_percent
  int64 state_age_ms
  string last_error
  ```
- `DispatcherState.msg` 末尾追加 `VehicleLinkState[] vda5050_vehicle_links`（替代评审否决的平行数组方案）。

### P0.5 强清安全边界（评审问题 6）
- 强清**不摘车**，改为**隔离**：`quarantined = true` → 该车**不再参与自动分配**（`PlanVehicleAssignment` 视为不合格），但仍在受管清单、仍可见、仍可被显式恢复。
- **恢复流程**：新增 `RestoreVda5050Link` 服务——需操作员确认车辆位置已核实（`position_verified` 字段）→ 清 `quarantined` → 重新参与分配。
- **审计**：`ForceClearVda5050Link.srv` 增加 `operator_id`（必填）、`reason`（必填）、`confirm_vehicle_id`（必须与 `vehicle_id` 完全一致，防误操作）。
- **服务端复验**：前端按钮隐藏**不是**安全边界；服务端 `PlanForceClearLink` 重新校验（在线车拒、隔离车拒、车辆 id 必须匹配）。
- **车辆物理占位未知**：强清释放锁前必须显式记录"车辆物理位置未核实"这一事实到审计日志（不伪称已确认安全）。

### P0.6 ROS 话题与 TF 隔离（评审坑 1、2）
- 话题命名：`/plan/{vid}`、`/cmd_vel_raw/{vid}`、`/cmd_vel_safe/{vid}`、`/odom/{vid}`、`/tracking/error/{vid}`。
- **vehicle_id 必须先过 ROS 名称校验**（`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`），非法 id 直接拒绝接入（外部 VDA 5050 serialNumber 不保证合法）。
- **TF frame 隔离**：每车 `odom_frame_id` / `base_frame_id` 唯一（如 `amr_01/odom`、`amr_01/base_link`），禁止多车抢同一 frame。
- 兼容红线：单车（`vehicle_ids` 为空）时**话题名逐字不变**。

### P0.7 并发派单原子性（评审坑 3）
- 派发链路的提交顺序固定为：**选车 → 占车（busy）→ 预留路权锁 → Pop 出队 → 发布订单/路径**。
- 任一步失败 → **逆序回滚**（释放 busy、回滚锁预留、任务留队），**禁止**出现"车被占但任务没派"或"锁被占但车没占"。
- 单线程 executor（现状 `rclcpp::spin`）保证无竞态，但**回滚必须写全**。

---

## Task A：真多车并发 + 显式绑定（评审后修订）

### A1 — 核心纯函数（已部分实现，按评审修订）
文件：`core/fleet/vehicle_assignment.hpp/.cpp`（已存在 `b6b3538`，需按 P0.3 修订）
- 修订点：①加 `backend`/`quarantined`/`position_valid`/`state_time` 字段；②结果改三态 `AssignmentOutcome`；③**删除** "first_available 兜底"（位置不可算 → 该车不合格）；④显式指定也施加全部硬约束；⑤加 `state_max_age_ms` 阈值（默认 5000，超龄 → 状态不确定 → `kIndeterminate`）。
- `test/unit/test_vehicle_assignment.cpp` 已有 24 例，需按新语义增补：三态各一例、隔离车不合格、位置无效不合格、状态超龄 → indeterminate、显式指定带全部硬约束。

### A2 — 车辆身份字段
- `mission_state.hpp`：`fleet_id` **保持原义**，**新增** `std::string assigned_vehicle_id;`
- `SubmitOrder.srv` / `EnqueueMission.srv`：末尾追加 `string assigned_vehicle_id`。
- `dispatcher_node.cpp`：`SubmitOrderCb` / `EnqueueMissionCb` 写入 `m.assigned_vehicle_id`。
- `rest_gateway.cpp`：`/api/v1/orders` 解析 `vehicle=` query 参数透传。

### A3 — 车队目录接入 + 车辆状态表
- `fleet.yaml`：`robots[]` 增 `backend` 字段（默认 `local_sim`）。
- `dispatcher_node`：`on_configure` 加载 `config/fleet.yaml`（参数 `fleet_catalog_file`），构建 `vehicle_states_`（vehicle_id → VehicleRuntimeState）。
- 动态刷新：VDA 5050 车从 `/fleet/{vid}/state` 更新 online/battery/position/state_time；本地车从 `/odom/{vid}` 更新位置。
- 隔离态：`quarantined` 由强清/恢复服务维护。

### A4 — per-vehicle 话题参数化（**仅 local_sim 后端的车**）
- `path_tracker_node`：参数 `vehicle_id`（默认空 = 单车兼容）+ 话题可覆盖。
- `safety_gate_node`：参数 `vehicle_id` + 话题可覆盖。
- `chassis_driver_node`：参数 `cmd_vel_topic` / `odom_topic` / frame 前缀。
- `dispatcher_node`：`plan_pub_` → `vehicle_plan_pubs_[vid]`；`/tracking/error/{vid}`、`/odom/{vid}` per-vehicle 订阅。
- `launch/full_system.launch.py`：`vehicle_ids` 参数（非空时按 local_sim 车起多组 tracker/gate/chassis，namespace 隔离）。

### A5 — 多车执行槽位拆分
- `tracking_mission_id_`（string）→ `tracking_missions_`（mission_id → vehicle_id）+ `vehicle_current_mission_`（vehicle_id → mission_id）。
- 派发门控：**只对 `kLocalSim` 车**要求 slot 空闲；`kVda5050` 车的"执行中"由订单状态判定，不占 path_tracker slot。
- `TrackingErrorCb`（local_sim 到达）按 vehicle_id 收口；VDA 5050 完成判定在 `Vda5050StateCb`（lastNodeId 到终点）。
- `EnforceVda5050LinkGuard`：fleet-wide 挂起 → **按车挂起**。

### A6 — 选车接线（tri-state）
- 派发时：`assigned_vehicle_id` 空 → 调 `PlanVehicleAssignment`。
  - `kAssigned` → 继续派发
  - `kDeferred` → **任务留队**（不 FailMission！），记 `pending_wait_`，下 tick 重试
  - `kIndeterminate` → 暂停自动派发（WARN），等状态恢复
  - `kRejected` → `FailMission` 带明确原因
- **队首阻塞**：队首任务不可派时，**继续扫描队列后续任务**找可派发的（需 core 支持 peek-N 或 snapshot 后逐个尝试）。

### A7 — 验证
- 核心单测：A1 修订后的用例 + A2 字段 + 派发 tri-state 决策单测。
- **e2e 回归（兼容红线）**：单车配置下现有 8 阶段原样 PASS。
- **e2e 新增 Stage 7（本地双模拟车）**：两台 local_sim 车各起一组 tracker/gate/chassis，提交 2 单 → 断言两车**同时**在跑（时间窗重叠断言）、状态不串线、锁无交叉误释放、两单都完成。
- **e2e 新增 Stage 8（双 VDA 5050 车）**：两台 mock VDA 车（`mock_amr_01`/`mock_amr_02`）+ 订单路由 → 断言两车各自收到 order、state 互不串线、两单都完成、锁正确释放。**不允许**用两套 ROS tracker 冒充 VDA 5050 多车闭环。

---

## Task C：Web 强清闭环（评审后修订）

### C1 — 服务语义修订
- `ForceClearVda5050Link.srv` 增：`operator_id`（必填）、`confirm_vehicle_id`（必填，须等于 `vehicle_id`）。
- 响应增：`quarantined`（车已隔离）、`audit_id`。
- 新增 `RestoreVda5050Link.srv`：`vehicle_id` + `operator_id` + `position_verified`（bool）→ 解除隔离。
- `PlanForceClearLink`（核心纯函数）按 P0.5 修订：在线拒、隔离拒、id 不匹配拒；受理 → 释锁 + 收口在途任务 + **置隔离**（非移除）。

### C2 — REST 端点
- `POST /api/v1/force_clear_link`，**请求体 JSON**（非 query）：`{vehicle_id, confirm_vehicle_id, operator_id, reason}`。
- `POST /api/v1/restore_link`：同上语义。
- `GET /api/v1/vehicle_links`：返回结构化车辆状态（复用 `VehicleLinkState`）。
- 危险操作：超时处理 + 审计字段透传 + 失败回传服务端拒绝原因（HTTP 409）。

### C3 — Web 控制台
- 新增「受管车辆」面板：表格（id / backend / online / busy / quarantined / 位置 / 电量 / 状态时延）。
- 强清按钮：**仅对满足服务端条件的车启用**（前端过滤是 UX，服务端仍复验）；点击后**弹确认框**要求填写 operator_id + reason，并回显车辆 id 确认。
- 隔离态展示 + 「恢复」按钮（需勾选"已核实车辆位置"）。
- 沿用现有 `baseUrl` + fetch 风格。

### C4 — 验证
- e2e Stage 6.8 扩展：改用 **REST 端点**触发强清，断言 HTTP 响应（含审计 id）+ 锁释放 + 车辆进入隔离 + 后续任务不派给该车。
- 新增：恢复流程断言（恢复后重新可派发）。
- 控制台手工验证。

---

## Task B：时空窗交通协调（评审后修订）

### B1 — 逐边进出时刻 + 全有或全无
- 核心新增 `core/workflow/time_space_planning.hpp/.cpp`：
  - 输入：每单的**逐资源**占用区间（每条边单独的 enter/exit 时刻）、资源冲突模型、车辆参数。
  - 占用时长 = 路径长度 / 速度 × 安全系数 + **加减速与转弯附加时间** + **车辆尺寸/安全余量**。
  - **全有或全无**：一条路径涉及多资源 → 必须**整条路径全部预约成功**才提交；任一失败 → 全部回滚（`ResourceTable` 需补一个批量预约接口，带 rollback）。
- 路口/窄道/对向冲突：进入资源模型（不只是同边窗口重叠）——**一期以"节点资源（路口）+ 边资源（通道）双粒度"表达**，节点窗口 = 进入路口到驶出路口的完整区间。

### B2 — 延期扩窗（执行偏离时）
- 车辆上报进度滞后 → **延长**该车的窗口（`ExtendTimeSpace`），延长失败（与后车窗口冲突）→ 触发**后车让行等待**（延后后车窗口），**绝不**因窗口到期而让后车进入。
- **窗口到期 ≠ 资源已释放**：释放仍需"车辆确认驶离该资源"（lastNodeId 推进），与 Spec §5.3 逐段解锁一致。

### B3 — 双模式接线
- 参数 `traffic_mode: static | time_space`（**默认 static**，现网行为不变）。
- `time_space` 模式仅在 Task A 多车并发落地且 B1/B2 单测全绿后**显式启用**。

### B4 — 验证
- `test/unit/test_time_space_planning.cpp`：逐边窗口、全有或全无回滚、延期扩窗、冲突让行、零时长边界。
- `test/integration/`：两单共享边不同窗口 → 双成功；同窗口 → 一成一败（无残留半预约）。

---

## 执行顺序与提交切分

```
P0（契约冻结：设计文档 + 核心类型 + srv/msg 变更）
 └→ A（多车并发 + 绑定 + 选车）
     └→ B（时空窗）
 C（Web 强清，可与 A 并行）
```

提交（每条带 `Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>`）：
1. `docs: 冻结多车车队化接口契约（执行后端/身份语义/选车三态/强清边界）`
2. `feat(core): 车辆执行后端与选车三态决策（PlanVehicleAssignment 修订）`
3. `feat(core): 强清隔离语义与审计字段（PlanForceClearLink 修订）`
4. `feat(interfaces): 结构化车辆状态消息与提单/强清/恢复服务契约`
5. `feat(ros): 车队目录接入与 per-vehicle 话题参数化（local_sim 后端）`
6. `feat(ros): 多车执行槽位拆分与按车挂起守卫`
7. `feat(ros): 选车接线（tri-state：留队/暂停/拒绝）`
8. `feat(web): REST 强清/恢复端点与结构化车辆状态`
9. `feat(web): Web 控制台受管车辆面板与强清/恢复交互`
10. `feat(core): 时空窗逐边预约决策与全有或全无提交`
11. `feat(ros): traffic_mode 双模式接线`

## 验证总表

| 项 | 命令 | 期望 |

| 核心单测 | `ctest --test-dir build/core` | 612 + 新增全绿 |

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option); the `model` parameter here overrides the definition for this one call.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative — "will I need this output again" — not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this — it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path — do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running — give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* — what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.

Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

For fresh agents, terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this — it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>

  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn — the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
<commentary>
A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.
</commentary>
Agent({
  name: "migration-review",
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes — I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
</example>

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - If you must poll an external process, use a check command (e.g. `gh run view`) rather than sleeping first.
  - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - If you must poll an external process, use a check command (e.g. `gh run view`) rather than sleeping first.
  - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.
- `cell_id` is the `id` attribute shown in the Read tool's `<cell id="...">` output. It is required for `replace` and `delete`.
- `edit_mode` defaults to `replace`. Use `insert` to add a new cell after the cell with the given `cell_id` (or at the beginning of the notebook if `cell_id` is omitted) — `cell_type` is required when inserting. Use `delete` to remove the cell.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
IMPORTANT: WebFetch WILL FAIL for authenticated or private URLs. Before using this tool, check if the URL points to an authenticated service (e.g. Google Docs, Confluence, Jira, GitHub). If so, look for a specialized MCP tool that provides authenticated access.

- Fetches content from a specified URL and processes it using an AI model
- Takes a URL and a prompt as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts HTML to markdown
- Processes the content with the prompt using a small, fast model
- Returns the model's response about the content
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: If an MCP-provided web fetch tool is available, prefer using that tool instead of this one, as it may have fewer restrictions.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - localhost and other hostnames without a dot are not supported; for a local server, use curl via Bash
  - The prompt should describe what information you want to extract from the page
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large
  - Includes a self-cleaning cache (entries expire after 15 minutes) for faster responses when repeatedly accessing the same URL
  - When a URL redirects to a different host, the tool will inform you and provide the redirect URL in a special format. You should then make a new WebFetch request with the redirect URL to fetch the content.
  - For GitHub URLs, prefer using the gh CLI via Bash instead (e.g., gh pr view, gh issue view, gh api).

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
- Allows Claude to search the web and use the results to inform responses
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Returns search result information formatted as search result blocks, including links as markdown hyperlinks
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond Claude's knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

CRITICAL REQUIREMENT - You MUST follow this:
  - After answering the user's question, you MUST include a "Sources:" section at the end of your response
  - In the Sources section, list all relevant URLs from the search results as markdown hyperlinks: [Title](URL)
  - This is MANDATORY - never skip including sources in your response
  - Example format:

    [Your answer here]

    Sources:
    - [Source Title 1](https://example.com/1)
    - [Source Title 2](https://example.com/2)

Usage notes:
  - Domain filtering is supported to include or block specific websites
  - Web search is only available in the US

IMPORTANT - Use the correct year in search queries:
  - The current month is October 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information, documentation, or current events.
  - Example: If the user asks for "latest React docs", search for "React documentation" with the current year, NOT last year
